SIF Engine

AI-Powered Industrial Safety Intelligence

Project Overview

SIF Engine is a machine learning safety intelligence tool tailored for industrial environments. It parses unstructured, human-written incident reports and classifies hazardous scenarios to alert safety managers to high-severity risks before incidents escalate.

Problem Statement

Industrial safety teams manually review hundreds of daily near-miss and unsafe-condition logs. Subtle linguistic cues indicating high-severity precursors are frequently overlooked in massive textual data, risking preventable industrial accidents.

Solution Approach

Built an end-to-end NLP and classification pipeline using FastAPI and custom spaCy / Sentence Transformer embeddings paired with Scikit-learn logistic regression models. The system evaluates incoming reports in real time, scores precursors, and presents risk indicators on a review dashboard.

System Architecture

Conceptual Processing Pipeline

1.Unstructured Safety Reports
2.Text Preprocessing & Tokenization (spaCy)
3.NLP & Feature Extraction (Sentence Transformers)
4.ML Classification (Scikit-learn Logistic Regression)
5.Risk Score & Precursor Extraction Engine
6.FastAPI REST Endpoints
7.React Safety Intelligence Dashboard

* Model outputs support safety professionals and do not replace qualified site assessments.

Implemented Features

  • Safety report severity classification
  • SIF precursor identification via NLP
  • Unsafe act & condition hazard tagging
  • Interactive human review workflow dashboard
  • FastAPI REST backend with SQLite persistence

Technical Decisions

  • Selected Logistic Regression over deep networks due to high interpretability for safety domain auditors.
  • Used spaCy pipelines for custom domain entity recognition and noise reduction.
  • Implemented SQLite with FastAPI to ensure low-latency operations and simple deployment.

Known Limitations

  • Model outputs serve as advisory indicators for safety officers, not automated replacements for qualified site inspections.
  • Requires domain-specific retraining for highly specialized industrial sub-sectors.
